edges.limitations: Homozygous region-specific deletion rather than the patients' heterozygous constitutional loss. The mouse cerebellum is small, whereas the most frequent cerebellar finding in patients is enlargement, so the model captures the c-Jun-dependent mechanism but not the patient phenotype.

evidence.snippet: The corpus callosum was absent, hypoplastic, or dysplastic in seven cases (41.2%).

nodes.description: Cerebellum-specific Fbxw7 deletion reduces cerebellar size and Purkinje cell number. Removing c-Jun or blocking its N-terminal phosphorylation rescues the Purkinje cell defect.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Cerebellar anomalies were seen in five individuals (29.4%), while delayed myelination, brainstem thickening, and polymicrogyria were each observed in 11.7%.

nodes.description: In fbxw7 mutant zebrafish, elevated Notch signaling makes spinal cord precursors produce too many oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Whether this contributes to the white matter and myelination anomalies seen in patients has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: Fbxw7 regulates Notch to control specification of neural precursors for oligodendrocyte fate.
evidence.snippet: Positional cloning revealed that the vu56 allele is a mutation of fbxw7, which encodes the substrate recognition component of a ubiquitin ligase that targets Notch and other proteins for degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Fbxw7 regulates Notch to control specification of neural precursors for oligodendrocyte fate.
evidence.snippet: the increase in OPC number resulted from production of extra OPCs by ventral spinal cord precursors and not from changes in OPC proliferation or death

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Collectively, the data presented herein provide compelling evidence of an F-Box protein-related, phenotypically variable neurodevelopmental disorder associated with monoallelic variants in FBXW7.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Reported germline variants include missense, frameshift, splice-site, and larger structural variants, with the majority clustering in the WD40 domain and disrupting substrate recognition.

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function FBXW7 variants, including whole-gene and regulatory-region copy number variants, nonsense, frameshift and splice-site variants, leave a single functional allele. Missense variants cluster at the substrate-binding surface of the WD40 propeller and are thought to act through loss of substrate recognition. Haploinsufficiency is the favored mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: F-box and WD repeat domain-containing 7 (FBXW7) encodes the substrate-recognition subunit of the SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, where it regulates proteasome-mediated degradation of key cell cycle and developmental proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We used a genotype-first approach and global data-sharing platforms to identify 35 individuals harboring de novo and inherited FBXW7 germline monoallelic chromosomal deletions and nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, and missense variants associated with a neurodevelopmental syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Haploinsufficiency or loss of function is currently considered the most likely pathogenic mechanism

evidence.reference_title: Copy number variants at 4q31.3 affecting the regulatory region of FBXW7 associated with neurodevelopmental delay.
evidence.snippet: We report two patients with a de novo deletion and a duplication in chromosome 4q31, potentially causing FBX-related neurodevelopmental syndrome by affecting the regulatory region of FBXW7.

evidence.reference_title: Reciprocal chromosome translocation t(3;4)(q27;q31.2) with deletion of 3q27 and reduced FBXW7 expression in a patient with developmental delay, hypotonia, and seizures.
evidence.snippet: FBXW7 expression in the immortalized lymphoblasts of the patient was reduced compared to that in controls.

nodes.description: Cerebellum-specific Fbxw7 knockout mice have a small cerebellum, fewer Purkinje cells with defective axonal arborization, supernumerary fissures and abnormal progenitor migration. Patients show the opposite direction: cerebellar enlargement is the most frequent posterior fossa finding on MRI (see the model-mismatch discussion), so this node is not linked to the patient imaging phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: The F-box protein Fbw7 is required for cerebellar development.
evidence.snippet: This resulted in decreased cerebellar size, reduced Purkinje cell number and defects in axonal arborisation.

nodes.description: Pan-neuronal knockdown of the Drosophila FBXW7 ortholog archipelago impairs learning and neuronal function, showing that reduced FBXW7 activity in neurons affects cognition independently of gross brain malformation.

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Pan-neuronal knockdown of the Drosophila ortholog, archipelago, impaired learning and neuronal function.

nodes.description: Reduced FBXW7 activity slows ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover of its phosphodegron-bearing substrates. Patient missense variants expressed in cultured cells fail to clear cyclin E1 and cyclin E2.

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Expression of recombinant FBXW7 missense variants in cultured cells demonstrated impaired CYCLIN E1 and CYCLIN E2 turnover.

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: A crystal-structure model of FBXW7 predicted that missense variants were clustered at the substrate-binding surface of the WD40 domain and that these might reduce FBXW7 substrate binding affinity.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated absence epilepsy associated with a de novo FBXW7 missense variant in the F-box domain.
evidence.snippet: Structural modeling predicted significant impairment in protein-protein binding affinity, particularly with the SCF complex component SKP1, supporting a potentially disruptive effect of the p.(Arg309Pro) substitution on complex assembly.

nodes.description: Intellectual disability ranges from borderline to severe and is mild to moderate in most individuals. The founding-cohort figure combines delay and intellectual disability; in a later seven-patient series formal intellectual disability was documented in four. A minority have normal cognition.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Mild to moderate DD or ID was observed in 77.1%, while 8.6% had severe GDD or ID.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding clinical variability in FBXW7-related neurodevelopmental disorder: a multicenter case series.
evidence.snippet: Formal intellectual disability was documented in four cases, while one individual showed preserved cognitive functioning with predominant behavioral difficulties.

nodes.description: NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 are degraded by SCF(FBXW7). When Fbxw7 is deleted from the mouse brain, NOTCH proteins accumulate in neural stem cells and NOTCH target genes are upregulated, prolonging stem-cell maintenance.

evidence.reference_title: Fbxw7-dependent degradation of Notch is required for control of "stemness" and neuronal-glial differentiation in neural stem cells.
evidence.snippet: The maintenance of neural stem cells was sustained in association with the accumulation of Notch1 and Notch3, as well as up-regulation of Notch target genes in the mutant mice.

nodes.description: Brain-specific homozygous Fbxw7 deletion causes neonatal death with brain malformation, NOTCH accumulation in neural stem cells and an astrocytic differentiation bias.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Cerebellar anomalies were seen in five individuals (29.4%), while delayed myelination, brainstem thickening, and polymicrogyria were each observed in 11.7%.

nodes.description: Fbxw7-deficient neural progenitors over-produce astrocytes at the expense of neurons, and brain-specific knockout mice show gross brain malformation and die shortly after birth.

evidence.reference_title: Fbxw7-dependent degradation of Notch is required for control of "stemness" and neuronal-glial differentiation in neural stem cells.
evidence.snippet: Astrogenesis was also enhanced in the mutant mice in vivo

nodes.description: FBXW7 is a tumor suppressor. In the few carriers who developed Wilms tumor, the tumor carried a somatic truncating variant on the other FBXW7 allele, giving biallelic inactivation in tumor tissue (a two-hit mechanism).

evidence.reference_title: Two-hit mutation causes Wilms tumor in an individual with FBXW7-related neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we detected a somatic nonsense variant on the paternal allele of FBXW7 in the tumor DNA.

evidence.reference_title: Further evidence that the neurodevelopmental gene FBXW7 predisposes to Wilms tumor.
evidence.snippet: In the tumor, we identified a second hit frameshift variant in FBXW7.

nodes.description: About three quarters of patients who had brain imaging showed structural anomalies, most often of the corpus callosum, the cerebellum and the cerebral white matter.

evidence.reference_title: Germline variants in tumor suppressor FBXW7 lead to impaired ubiquitination and a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Brain imaging detailed variable underlying structural abnormalities affecting the cerebellum, corpus collosum, and white matter.

evidence.reference_title: FBXW7-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: reported imaging in 17 individuals, with abnormalities in 13 (76.5%).

nodes.description: Wilms tumor has been reported in a few carriers of germline or constitutional mosaic FBXW7 variants, each with a somatic second hit in the tumor. Penetrance appears low.

evidence.reference_title: Further evidence that the neurodevelopmental gene FBXW7 predisposes to Wilms tumor.
evidence.snippet: we now observed a patient with neurodevelopmental delay due to a de novo constitutional mosaic FBXW7 splice site pathogenic variant who developed Wilms tumor.

evidence.reference_title: Two-hit mutation causes Wilms tumor in an individual with FBXW7-related neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel constitutional pathogenic variant of FBXW7 in a patient with intellectual disability, who also developed Wilms tumor.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding clinical variability in FBXW7-related neurodevelopmental disorder: a multicenter case series.
evidence.snippet: Wilms tumor was documented in two previously reported patients, with biallelic FBXW7 inactivation demonstrated in tumor tissue, supporting a biologically plausible but apparently low-penetrance cancer predisposition signal

nodes.description: N-terminally phosphorylated c-Jun is an SCF(FBXW7) substrate. Deleting both Fbxw7 alleles from the developing mouse cerebellum raises its level, together with NOTCH1, and this c-Jun excess is responsible for Purkinje cell loss and poor arborization.

evidence.reference_title: The F-box protein Fbw7 is required for cerebellar development.
evidence.snippet: Protein levels of the Fbw7 substrates Notch1 and N-terminally phosphorylated c-Jun were upregulated in fbw7(∆Cb) mice.
